review_notes:
I read the whole file. It is a generated certificate file with four parts. First comes a data table (`CA4_6_6I1PairCertificates`). Then come an index `match` and 36 lemmas `CA4_6_6I1PairP_check_i_j`, each proved by `decide +kernel`. Last come a short chain of soundness lemmas. I also looked up `forall_fin6` in SparseContraction.lean. It is a small helper that finishes by `fin_cases i <;> assumption`.

The 36 check lemmas and the 36-argument dispatch in `CA4_6_6I1PairP_check` look repetitive. But they contain no repeated nontrivial mathematical reasoning. Each lemma is a closed finite kernel computation. The split into 36 pieces looks like a deliberate way to keep each kernel check small. I could not verify that without running Lean. Merging them into one parameterised lemma would be a routine restructuring of a decision procedure, and I could not show that it would compile or cost the same. The rubric excludes this kind of change: it calls for nontrivial repeated reasoning and rejects thin wrappers and routine unfolding.

The soundness chain (`..._sound`, `..._valid`, `..._Entropy_sound`, `..._Mass_sound`, `..._H_sound`) is a sequence of single applications of shared API lemmas: `contains_sound`, `stageAPairBall_sound`, `entropyDoublePair_enclosed`, `doublePairSumBall_sound`, `entropyTerm_ball` and `homogeneous_enclosed`. These are already factored into those lemmas. I found no repeated proof block in this file that would justify a new shared lemma with both rewritten uses.

I did not search the other CapacityA files for the same pattern. That is the only remaining uncertainty.
